{{Short description|none}} 

{{Use dmy dates|date=January 2025}} 

This '''Brazilian [[Association football|football]] champions''' are the winners of the competitions recognized by [[Brazilian Football Confederation]] (CBF) as the [[Campeonato Brasileiro Série A]], the top-flight football league of Brazil.

In 1933, the [[Federação Paulista de Futebol|São Paulo State Football Federation]] and the [[Federação de Futebol do Estado do Rio de Janeiro|Rio de Janeiro State Football Federation]] decided to create the [[Torneio Rio–São Paulo]] between teams from the two states. In 1937, the [[1937 Brazilian Football Championship|Torneio dos Campeões]] was disputed between four state champions teams from the [[Southeast Region, Brazil|Southeast region]]. In 1959, the [[Brazilian Sports Confederation|CBD]] (the predecessor of the CBF) created the [[Taça Brasil]] with the objective of sending a representative club from the country to the [[1960 Copa Libertadores|inaugural Copa Libertadores]]. In 1966, the São Paulo and Rio de Janeiro state federations decided to expand Torneio Rio–São Paulo to the states of [[Minas Gerais]], [[Paraná (state)|Paraná]], and [[Rio Grande do Sul]], and renamed it the [[Torneio Roberto Gomes Pedrosa]], a change which took place in 1967. In 1969, the CBD discontinued the Taça Brasil and began organizing the Torneio Roberto Gomes Pedrosa, calling it the Taça de Prata some times.

In 1971, influenced by the ''Programa de Integração Nacional'' of the [[Military dictatorship in Brazil|military regime]], the CBD renamed the competition to Campeonato Nacional de Clubes, maintaining the same tournament format.<ref name="FGV">{{cite web|access-date=9 June 2016|publisher=Fundação Getúlio Vargas|title=Futebol e política: a criação do Campeonato Nacional de Clubes de Futebol|url=http://bibliotecadigital.fgv.br/dspace/bitstream/handle/10438/10367/Futebol%20e%20pol%C3%ADtica-a%20cria%C3%A7%C3%A3o%20do%20campeonato%20brasileiro%20de%20clubes%20de%20futebol.pdf?sequence=1|archive-date=15 September 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160915165214/http://bibliotecadigital.fgv.br/dspace/bitstream/handle/10438/10367/Futebol%20e%20pol%C3%ADtica-a%20cria%C3%A7%C3%A3o%20do%20campeonato%20brasileiro%20de%20clubes%20de%20futebol.pdf?sequence=1|url-status=live}}<!-- auto-translated by Module:CS1 translator --></ref><ref name="trivela.uol.com.br">{{Cite web |date=2017-10-21|title=O futebol também foi uma obra faraônica dos militares, e sofremos com isso até hoje - Trivela|work=Trivela|url=http://trivela.uol.com.br/o-futebol-tambem-foi-uma-obra-faraonica-dos-militares-e-esses-exageros-fazem-efeito-ate-hoje/|access-date=2023-10-21|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171021062046/http://trivela.uol.com.br/o-futebol-tambem-foi-uma-obra-faraonica-dos-militares-e-esses-exageros-fazem-efeito-ate-hoje/|archive-date=21 October 2017}}</ref> Since then, different names was adopted and all subsequent editions have been organized by the CBD/CBF, with the exception of the [[Copa União|1987 Copa União]] and the [[2000 Campeonato Brasileiro Serie A|2000 edition]] organized by the [[Clube dos 13]], but recognized later by the CBF. 

On 13 December 2010, the CBF additionally recognized the winners of the [[Taça Brasil]] (1959–1968) and the [[Torneio Roberto Gomes Pedrosa]] (1967–1970) as Brazilian football champions. It has also briefely recognized the [[Controversy over the title of the 1987 Brazilian football champion|1987 controversial edition]] as an edition with two champions, but was forced to backtrack on this decision later.<ref>{{cite web |last1=do Carmo Fernandes Pais |first1=Maria |title=Unificação dos Títulos Brasileiros a partir de 1959 |url=http://docplayer.com.br/9676794-Unificacao-dos-titulos-brasileiros-a-partir-de-1959.html |website=docplayer.com.br |access-date=17 February 2020 |language=pt-br |format=pdf}}</ref><ref name="1959-1970">{{cite web |title=CBF iguala Taça Brasil e 'Robertão' a Brasileiro. Santos e Palmeiras viram octas |url=http://globoesporte.globo.com/futebol/noticia/2010/12/cbf-equipara-taca-brasil-e-robertao-brasileiro-santos-e-palmeiras-viram-octas.html |website=globoesporte.globo.com |access-date=17 February 2020 |language=pt-br |date=13 December 2010}}</ref><ref name="Conmebol">{{cite web |url=http://www.conmebol.com/conmebol/mainMedia.html?id=17886&viewpage='full' |title=Unification of titles in Brazil recognizes the glories of Pelé's Santos and Palmeiras |publisher=[[CONMEBOL]] |access-date=December 26, 2010 |date=December 23, 2010 }}</ref> In 25 August 2023, the [[1937 Brazilian Football Championship|1937 Torneio dos Campeões]] was also recognized as an official title.<ref name="Atlético1937">{{cite web|url=https://ge.globo.com/futebol/times/atletico-mg/noticia/2023/08/25/e-tri-cbf-reconhece-atletico-mg-como-campeao-brasileiro-de-1937.ghtml |title=É tri! CBF reconhece Atlético-MG como campeão brasileiro de 1937 |website=GloboEsporte |date=25 August 2023 |language=pt}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.itatiaia.com.br/editorias/atletico/2023/08/25/veja-o-elenco-do-atletico-que-conquistou-o-brasileirao-de-1937 |title=Veja o elenco do Atlético que conquistou o Brasileirão de 1937 |website=Itatiaia |date=25 August 2023 |language=pt}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.rsssfbrasil.com/tablesrz/tbrtops.htm |title=Taça Brasil -- List of Topscorers |publisher=RSSSF Brazil |first=Paulo |last=Torres |date=August 11, 2000 |access-date=December 25, 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120103185750/http://rsssfbrasil.com/tablesrz/tbrtops.htm |archive-date=January 3, 2012 |df=mdy-all }}</ref>

Since its first edition, 17 different clubs have won the league.
